content: The Australian Medicines Handbook (AMH) is a widely utilized medical reference text among healthcare professionals in Australia, particularly general practitioners and pharmacists. It is highly regarded for its concise and independent drug information, which supports the practice of evidence-based medicine. The AMH is modeled after the British National Formulary (BNF) but contains entirely Australian-specific content. It is published by an independent company, Australian Medicines Handbook Pty Ltd, based in Adelaide, South Australia. The concept of the AMH was first proposed in 1991 as a collaborative effort between the Australian Society of Clinical and Experimental Pharmacologists and Toxicologists (ASCEPT), the Pharmaceutical Society of Australia (PSA), and the Royal Australian College of General Practitioners (RACGP). These organizations continue to sponsor its production. After seven years of development and with the assistance of a Commonwealth grant, the first edition was published in May 1998. Initially, it was released biennially (1998, 2000, and 2002 editions), but since 2002, it has been published annually. The current print edition, the eighth in the series, is the Australian Medicines Handbook 2007, which was released in January 2007. The AMH is also available in electronic formats, including eAMH for Microsoft Windows and Mac OS X platforms, accessible via CD-ROM and online through the Health Communication Network. Additionally, a version for personal digital assistants (PDAs), known as pAMH, is available for devices running on the Windows Mobile (Pocket PC) platform. The Australian Medicines Handbook also publishes two companion texts: the AMH Drug Choice Companion: Emergency and Primary Care and the AMH Drug Choice Companion: Aged Care. These texts focus on pharmacotherapeutics in specialized areas such as emergency medicine, primary care, and aged care. Past editions of the AMH include the following: Misan GM (Ed.) (1998).
